articles.title: Patrick Mahomes faces new Chiefs concern as Kenneth Walker’s status for Bills game remains uncertain
articles.standfirst: The Kansas City Chiefs could face a major setback ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs could face a major setback ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have handled running back Kenneth Walker III ’s return with extreme caution, gradually working him back into action after his injury.

However, a potential absence for Walker in this week’s crucial matchup against the Buffalo Bills could raise serious red flags inside the organization and become a bigger concern for Kansas City as the season winds down, according to one analyst.

Kenneth Walker could become a larger problem for the Chiefs

Joshua Brisco of SI.com responded to a fan’s question about the Chiefs’ plan if Walker is unable to play Thursday night against Buffalo. While the running back appears close to returning, the analyst warned that any new setback could carry significant consequences.

“To fully wade into a hypothetical that might be irrelevant by the time Tuesday’s injury report comes out: If Walker doesn’t play in Buffalo, I think you have to have some level of concern about his timeline and expectations for the rest of the year, simply due to the possibility that a short-term injury, downplayed by the team, could be lingering much longer than the player and team expected,” Brisco wrote.

“That’s always alarming until the player returns and looks like their pre-injury self.”

Kansas City received positive news on Tuesday when Kenneth Walker III returned to practice , though his participation against the Bills is still not guaranteed.

Head coach Andy Reid explained that the running back would not receive a heavy workload during his return to the practice field.

“We’ll see how he does. I’m not anticipating a ton of work there but he’ll get out there and move around,” Reid said.

The Chiefs may adjust their offensive approach

Walker’s situation could force the Chiefs to place greater emphasis on the run game against Buffalo, particularly given the weather expected for the Thanksgiving matchup.

The forecast calls for cold temperatures and strong winds, with the possibility of a winter storm producing gusts of up to 50 miles per hour—a factor that could limit the passing attacks of both teams.

In that scenario, Kansas City could increase the workload of rookie running back Emmett Johnson , who has performed well in Walker’s absence.

With Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs fighting to stay near the top of the AFC standings , Walker’s progress will be one of the most closely watched storylines ahead of the Buffalo game.

articles.title: Brittany and Patrick Mahomes' kids have their royal moment at the Kansas City Current parade
articles.standfirst: The team's celebration featured some adorable moments that stole the spotlight beyond the soccer field.
articles.summary: The team's celebration featured some adorable moments that stole the spotlight beyond the soccer field.
articles.body:
B rittany Mahomes had plenty of reasons to join the festivities on Tuesday, November 24 . The Kansas City Current co-owner celebrated the franchise's first NWSL championship, secured with a 2-1 victory over the Washington Spirit in Saturday's final, November 21, at Audi Field in Washington, D.C.

And while the championship was the main attraction of the day, two special guests also caught everyone's attention during the parade through the streets of Kansas City: her children, Sterling and Bronze.

Brittany and Patrick Mahomes' kids get their royal moment

The little ones rode alongside their mom on one of the parade vehicles . Wearing Current jerseys, caps and sweatshirts, they waved to the fans gathered along the streets, looking up at them as the children enjoyed the celebration from above, like true members of royalty.

Brittany shared some of these moments on her Instagram Stories, but one scene featuring Sterling stood out from the rest. The little girl was fascinated as a shower of colorful confetti burst into the air and filled the sky. Her look of amazement was one of the sweetest moments of the day.

Randi Mahomes also joins the celebration

The family was also represented by Randi Mahomes, Patrick's mother, who joined Brittany for the parade .

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback couldn't attend because of his NFL commitments, but his absence didn't stop Brittany from sharing the celebration with other members of the family.

articles.title: Randi Mahomes opens up about her pride in Brittany and the example she sets for her granddaughters
articles.standfirst: After the KC Current won its first NWSL title, Patrick Mahomes’ mother celebrated her daughter-in-law’s hard work
articles.summary: After the KC Current won its first NWSL title, Patrick Mahomes’ mother celebrated her daughter-in-law’s hard work
articles.body:
R andi Mahomes had more than congratulations to share after the Kansas City Current won its first NWSL championship . In a heartfelt message, she said she was proud of Brittany and “all the hard work and love she has put into the KC Current from the very beginning.”

Celebrating the team’s title with her family made the moment even more special, Randi wrote. She loves watching Brittany’s dreams come true and knows that when her daughter-in-law is happy, her son Patrick Mahomes and her grandchildren are happy, too.

A championship years in the making

Brittany Mahomes helped launch the KC Current in 2020 and is a co-owner of the club. The team’s first league title came on Nov. 21, when it beat the Washington Spirit, 2-1. For Randi, the win carried a personal meaning: she had watched Brittany invest years of work and care in the team, then got to celebrate the result alongside her family.

Patrick Mahomes’ mother joined her daughter-in-law and the rest of the family in Kansas City to celebrate the championship. In her message, Randi praised Brittany’s dedication to the Current and the example she sets for her daughters.

The title was a milestone for Brittany as a co-owner and a proud moment for Randi, who had watched her work toward this dream.

Patrick Mahomes couldn’t attend the championship game because the Chiefs played the next day. He celebrated the KC Current’s win online and wore the team’s shirt to the Chiefs game. Afterward, he said it was “really cool” to see the players’ hard work pay off.

Randi’s message showed how much she wants her daughter-in-law to be happy and supported. She has watched Brittany work toward this dream for years, so seeing her celebrate the championship with her daughters meant a lot. As their grandmother, Randi was proud to share the moment with them.
